newsitem.title: USA: US OPTIONS FOCUS/Speculation in Micron, Morris up.
newsitem.headline: US OPTIONS FOCUS/Speculation in Micron, Morris up.

text.p: Speculation in Micron Technology Inc and Philip Morris Cos Inc increased on Monday for two distinctly different reasons, traders said.

Speculation in Micron was related to its quarterly earnings report, due after the close of trading, and in Philip Morris to a possible tobacco industry deal this week with several states attorneys general, traders said.
"It's all a play on what they say this afternoon," Rob Kovell of Kovell Trading LP said of Micron options activity on the Pacific Stock Exchange.
In late trading, Micron shares were up 1-1/4 at 42 on volume of more than 2.5 million shares.
Among the options, the June 42-1/2 call was most active, with total turnover of 3,570 contracts. The June 40 puts traded about 3,525 and the June 40 call about 2,855.
"We've had a good deal of put buyers probably speculating on bad numbers after what Intel said," Kovell said.
He added that over the last couple of weeks one investor had been a large buyer of the June 40 puts, which had open interest of 18,055 contracts.
At the end of May, Intel said its second quarter earnings would fall short of Wall Street expecations, largely because of weaker-than-expected demand, especially in Europe.

Kovell said Micron's actual earnings number--Wall Street analysts are forecasting on average profits of $0.39 a share, up from $0.27 in the year ago quarter--will not likely be as important as any comments the company makes.
"I think the most important thing to look at when the number comes out is what they have to say about demand," he said, adding that the stock appears to have room on both the downside and the upside.

Implied volatility in Micron options remained high, in the upper-60 to low-70 region, but down about 10 points from the levels reached when the investor was heavily buying the June 40 puts, Kovell said.
Implied volatility in Philip Morris and other tobacco companies was reaching historic levels on speculation the industry would reach an agreement with states attorneys general this week.
The attorneys general are suing the industry to recoup costs of treating diseases allegedly caused by smoking.
Sources close to talks between the industry and the state officials said a deal is possible this week.

"We're seeing volatility at almost historic levels," said Andrew Schwarz at AGS Specialist Partners. "Everybody is speculating that some sort of agreement will be reached this week and they're speculating through the options."
For Philip Morris, where a July 45/50 call spread was bought by an institution 8,000 times, that meant volatility of around 60 for the June series.
The June 45 call traded 12,625 contracts and the June 50 call traded nearly 13,000 in late action.
